# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why7: The box asks for 1 to 4 benefits of up to 9 words, each one compared with today's way, with *I'm not sure* as the founder's escape; my two rows are each one gain, don't overlap and are within the limit.

screens.why1: Right after I typed what Fresco does better, it's obvious Keel shows me back its two rows to check before it tests them.
screens.why2: "Hours back at the end of the day" and "action items to the crew the same day" are how supers and I talk about it; I read both rows on first pass.
screens.why3: Both rows are what a super lives with: the hours in the trailer after the walk, and getting punch items out to the crew before tomorrow.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, one for time and one for getting items to the crew, under 9 words each, no number I didn't write, and they cover my pitch (done during the walk, not after; 90% faster).
screens.why5: Both benefits are mine in substance, "hours back" for the 90%-faster claim and "action items to the crew" for texting the crew, and the lead one comes first.
screens.why7: Both rows are carried into the belief joined with *and*, in my order; but the belief's occasion is "their last daily log" while revision 25 moved the occasion to the site walk, and a daily log "giving them action items to the crew the same day" bends the hard case the advantage is for.
screens.instead: Keep both rows; Keel will test: For most, with it, their last site walk would have given them hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day.

screens.why1: Right after what it does better comes what it costs my supers to start using it, which is the obvious next question about the solution.
screens.why2: "What will they have to do to start using it?" and "setup, extra steps or learning" are plain to me on the first read.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super has to change: say who owns each item while filming, and review the notes before they go to the crew and Procore.
screens.why4: A free box with the four-row, nine-word limit and an *I'm not sure* chip that leaves the dimension out is all this screen needs, and the escape fits.
screens.why5: My two efforts sit in the box as I typed them, nothing reworded.
screens.why7: The box asks for one to four efforts of at most nine words, matching the card; both of my rows are base-form steps the super takes himself (a new habit of use, not a sign-off or a fit with Procore, which other screens test); and the *I'm not sure* escape is there.

screens.why1: Right after I said what supers will have to do to start, Keel shows me the efforts it drafted from my answer, so it is obvious why this list is here.
screens.why2: Naming who owns each item and checking the notes before they go out to the crew are how a super talks about a punch walk and a daily log.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does himself on the walk or in the trailer, so he can say whether he would do them.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, one a habit while filming and one a review of the output, each under nine words in the supers' own voice, with no overlap or odd row.
screens.why5: It keeps my mechanism of narrated video with assignees texted to the crew, and the check step answers the hallucination worry the sceptics raised, without drifting from what I typed.
screens.why7: Both rows are base-form efforts the superintendent takes himself, a new habit of use, not another role's sign-off or a Compatibility or Purchase friction condition, within 1 to 4 and nine words, so a Yes or a No answers the belief.
screens.instead: Keep both rows and add the core habit as a third: Film short clips and talk over them on the walk.

screens.why1: Right after I checked my adoption-effort rows, I'm asked which one effort the strangers get tested on, so it's obvious why it's here.
screens.why2: 'Name who owns each item as they film' and 'check and fix the notes before they go out' are how a super talks about a walk and a punch list, plain on first read.
screens.why3: Both are things a superintendent does with their own hands and mouth on the walk or in the trailer, answerable from their own day.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, both theirs and in field words, with no overlap or nonsense row; Keel's optional suggested step is simply absent, which the card allows.
screens.why5: Naming owners matches the assignees in my pitch, but the effort I'd have said first, shooting short videos and talking over them on the walk, has slid into a sub-step ('as they film') since revision 25 moved it out, so the list drifted a little from what I typed.
screens.why7: Both rows are one-effort base-form steps the super takes themselves in 'their' voice, under 9 words, not another role's sign-off and not a Compatibility or Purchase-friction condition; the belief 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' can hold or fail on Yes/Only if versus Probably not/No, and the stranger-side I can't tell is the card's.
screens.instead: Which effort is most likely to stop them? -- Say who owns each item out loud as they film it / Check and fix the notes before they go out to the crew

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the obvious place to decide whether to ask supers for a pilot, and I want pilot sites, so it fits.
screens.why2: Pilot is the word I use myself (paid pilot on one site), and the hint says plainly what respondents will see and where I'll find the yeses.
screens.why3: Whether I want early users' emails is my own call as the founder; I know the answer without guessing.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, the two are distinct, and no escape is needed for a founder's own setting.
screens.why5: My pilot is a paid one on one site sold to the contractor, but the respondent's line 'Would you try this for real? Leave your email.' goes to supers who don't pay, so it collects interest from users and not a pilot in my sense, a small drift from what I typed.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? Respondents who say yes get: 'Would you try this on one of your jobs? Leave your email.' -- Yes, ask them / No pilot

screens.why1: Choosing who asks my superintendents the questions is the natural last setup step before the link goes out by text, right after the pilot offer.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint packs video, voice, credits and recording into one long paragraph, and 'tap Saskia to hear her and switch' reads as if hearing her also switches me.
screens.why3: I know my supers take calls in loud trailers and trucks, so I can judge which voice they'd sit through.
screens.why4: Two named voices with five-second samples is a workable choice, but the names alone say nothing about tone, pace or accent, so I can't tell them apart without playing both.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco or my roles leaks into this screen, and it does what I chose: keep Keel's preselected interviewer and record it once.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? Daphne (picked for you, calm and steady, ▶ 5 s) or Saskia (brighter and quicker, ▶ 5 s). Playing a sample doesn't switch; the voice you pick is recorded once, 400 credits either way.

screens.why1: Right after picking who asks the questions, choosing how the supers answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: AI interviewer, read and tap, let them choose: plain to me, and each option says in one line what the super would actually do.
screens.why3: I know my supers: they're on a phone in the trailer or truck at day's end, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk to a video.
screens.why4: The three options are complete and distinct, and my pick, Read and tap, is there in plain words; no escape is needed on a setup choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco leaks in, and my pick of Read and tap reads back as I chose it.

screens.why1: After choosing how superintendents answer, choosing who receives the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: The three options are plain to me as a founder; 'Contacts page' is Keel's own term but the description explains it.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I know by name from our pilots and intros, or posting in a group, so I can answer this from my own situation.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-sourced list, and an open group link are distinct and cover the realistic ways I'd reach superintendents, and an escape isn't needed for a founder's routing choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles is altered here, and my pick of people I know by name is kept.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated with '4 counted · 5 needed' on each card, but the headline pins it only to Compatibility while all three cards share the same count, so the deciding number reads oddly tied to one card.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart on the stage page, only a text tally; I can see 4 of 7 counted and a bar of 5, but I need a second look to see that 7 answered and only 4 counted on every card.
screens.why_b3: The dimensions are mine, and the narrated videos, Procore/ACC and hours back are my claims, but the beliefs are reworded (talking 'over the noise', 'name who owns each item') and the statement repeats itself ('gets back the notes with photos, assignees and due dates').
screens.why_b4: It tells me nothing can be called yet, but not what to do: send to more supers, or why three of seven weren't counted.
screens.why_b5: It makes no claim beyond the people who answered; n is visible and the low count is said plainly as too few to call.

screens.why_b1: Too few to call sits right beside 4 counted and 5 needed, so I know where it stands and the exact reason.
screens.why_b2: The bars read plainly as 3 for and 1 against, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' mixes the floor of 5 with the 2-in-3 rule, so I had to look twice to see where my bar actually sits.
screens.why_b3: The belief is recognisably mine, but it drops 'on commercial jobs', and the question asks about my last daily log, not the site walk where the noise actually is.
screens.why_b4: Asking Ray why he said No is a concrete step, but the screen never says I need just one more counted answer to call it, and the closing quote about the deck not waiting has nothing to do with noise.
screens.why_b5: The small n is stated plainly ('a lean, not a call'), but framing the question around the daily log, which happens in the trailer, could mislead me about what people were answering on site noise.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 could talk over the noise on their last site walk; one more answer settles it, so get one more super and ask Ray what drowned him out.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside the number that decides it: 4 counted, 5 needed to call it.
screens.why_b2: The chart's counts are plain (3 a lot better, 0 a little, 1 same, 1 of 4 against), but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* mixes the 5-person floor with the 1-in-3 bar, so I had to read it twice to see that my bar is about the against share and not about 4 of 5 saying yes.
screens.why_b3: The dimension name and the belief line are mine, with both benefits (hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day), though the bar line *You said hours back at the end of the day* quotes only the first.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted super decides it, or that the lean so far is 3 a lot better against Denise's no difference.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart, and the screen calls it *a lean, not a call* rather than claiming it held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted said a lot better and 1 (Denise, who finishes her log on site) said no difference, so the lean is for you; one more counted super decides it, and the bar is no more than 1 in 3 against, not 4 of 5.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside its deciding numbers, *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know the result and why at once.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 1 Yes, 2 Only if, 1 Probably not and 0 No over 5 answered, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* with the marker at 4 reads like a 4-of-5 threshold, which clashes with the rule *no more than 1 in 3 say probably not or no*, so I have to look twice to see where my bar sits.
screens.why_b3: *Adoption friction* and *Most would name who owns each item as they film* are the dimension and the step I picked; naming the assignee as I film is how Fresco builds its notes.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic: it doesn't tell me I need one more counted super, or that the lean for me hangs on *only if it keeps my walk moving*, which is the thing my product has to prove.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted, Luis out as a guess), and the screen calls the small group *a lean, not a call* without overclaiming 3 of 4.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of the 5 needed are counted. 3 lean yes, but 2 of them only if naming owners doesn't slow the walk. Get one more super's answer, and show in the pilot that tagging an owner takes seconds.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know the answer is not yet in and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Both names and belief lines are the ones I checked: 'could talk into their phone over the noise on site' (the r25 wording) and hours back at end of day plus action items to the crew the same day.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more answer, but nothing says what to do or what these single no's mean for the walk-and-talk mechanism or the time-back pitch.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the low count is said outright, each quote is shown as a single against (1 of 1 asked), and nothing is called strong or weak beyond that.
screens.why_b6: I did not type that Ray's no had nothing to do with site noise (the log just loses to a slipping schedule) or that Denise's log is already done on the tablet before the gate, so for her the pain is subs and the schedule, not the log.

screens.why1: As the opening screener, it makes sense to first check whether my jobs log dailies in software before asking about getting photos and notes into the log.
screens.why2: Daily logs and construction management software are everyday words on a GC job, though in the trailer I'd just say Procore.
screens.why3: I know exactly where my jobs keep their dailies, so I can answer straight off.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, and asking about 'any' of my jobs handles a mix of jobs on Procore and jobs on paper.
screens.why5: Nothing about the founder's product or plan reaches me; it only asks about the tool my jobs already use.
screens.why6: It is short and one question, but 'I'll read 2 options. Yes; or No.' sounds stiff for a yes-or-no gate, where §17 says to end with just 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you're running now keep their daily logs in Procore, ACC or similar software? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs keep logs in software, asking whether I lost notes before writing the log is the obvious next thing to check.
screens.why2: It's my words, but 'lose site notes' makes me stop and ask: lost the notepad, or forgot what I saw on the walk by the time I sat down in the trailer?
screens.why3: I know whether I lost anything between the walk and the log this week; it's my own daily routine.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but losing notes is a narrower pain than the hours spent getting photos and notes into the log, so the count may drift from what the founder meant.
screens.why6: One short sentence then 'Yes or no.' is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Two fixed answers in order with no escape on the gate, and it's a real failure some supers say No to and some Yes, so the belief can be supported or refuted.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs run logs in software and whether I lost notes before writing the daily log, showing me the idea at the start of Part 2 makes sense.
screens.why2: Site walk, Procore, ACC, crew, action items and due dates are how I talk; 'scribe' isn't my word, but I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day with my phone and put photos and notes into Procore, so I can picture this.
screens.why4: A card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: The belief line, 'it would be your scribe during the site walk', just repeats the name and says nothing about what it would do for me, like saving the hours of uploading or getting the daily log right, and the card never mentions the daily log the last screen asked about.
screens.why6: Short sentences that say well; ACC and Procore are said as names on any job, and the one list of photos, assignees and due dates is easy to hold.
screens.instead: Keep the first two paragraphs, and end with: The people building it believe it would save you the hours of uploading photos and writing up the daily log after the walk.

screens.why1: Right after the Fresco card it makes sense to ask whether I could even talk into my phone out there, since that's what the whole idea rests on.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but 'think of your last daily log' made me stop: I write the log in the trailer at the end of the day, and the talking would happen on the walk, so I had to work out that they meant the walk behind that log.
screens.why3: I know exactly how loud it gets with saws, a lift beeping and a pump running, and whether I could have narrated over it.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, only sometimes, no covers it for a noisy site, nothing overlaps, and I can't tell fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Only the idea card shows Fresco, as it should, and the question itself is in site words with nothing of the founder's plan creeping in.
screens.why6: One short question, four short options said as a list, then the one escape, easy to hold on a single hearing.
screens.why7: It's an ability on the one measure, could I have, with the card's four in order (two for, two against) plus I can't tell apart, and it tests the step the pitch depends on, which will be true for some supers and false for others.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the talking-over-noise question, it makes sense to ask whether Fresco would have beaten how I did my last log.
screens.why2: "The last daily log when you had to keep an accurate record of the day's work on site" is stiff; every log is that, so I'd read it twice looking for what day they mean, and "done that better" doesn't say better at what: faster, fewer missed items, or less time uploading to Procore.
screens.why3: I write a daily log every day, so I can answer whether something that turned my walk footage into notes would have helped.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference, worse, with I can't tell set apart, covers it cleanly with no overlap.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks beyond the idea card, but the stem reads like someone else's phrasing ("keep an accurate record of the day's work on site") rather than how a super talks, and "site-walk videos" assumes video when most of us shoot photos.
screens.why6: Heard aloud it's two long sentences with Fresco's full description repeated, so by the time the four options come I've half lost what "that" was, though the options themselves say well.
screens.why7: The measure, the four fixed options in order, the balance and the I can't tell escape are all right, but the occasion is any last log rather than the hard case the advantage is for, such as the day notes got lost or the log was needed for a delay dispute.
screens.instead: Think of the last day you lost site notes before writing the daily log. Would Fresco have made that log better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: After asking whether I could talk into my phone and whether Fresco would do my log better, asking what extra I'd have to do on the walk to use it comes naturally as the last idea question.
screens.why2: "Name who owns each item" takes me a second; on site I'd say "call out which sub is responsible" for each issue, and "item" doesn't say whether it's a punch item, a note or something else.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day and already know which sub or crew each issue belongs to, so I can say whether I'd call that out while filming.
screens.why4: Yes, the conditional yes, probably not and no are distinct and complete, and "only if it keeps my walk moving" is the real catch for me, with I can't tell fitting as the escape.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks beyond the idea card shown on purpose, and the step reads as a plain thing the tool would ask of me on the walk.
screens.why6: Short stem, one question, four short options and one escape, easy to hold on one hearing.
screens.why7: The effort is a new habit I'd take on myself while filming, the four fixed answers are in order with a for-and-against balance, the conditional is a specific assurance about this step and not a fear, and I can't tell sits apart as required.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd say out loud which sub is responsible for each issue as you film. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Only if it keeps my walk moving · Probably not · No · I can't tell
